candidate.answerReason: Relative to the raft, the boat moves away and returns at the same speed. It must therefore spend equal times before and after turning, dividing the nine-hour trip into two 4.5-hour parts.

methods.label: Measure from the raft
methods.explanation:
The raft moves with the current, so measuring the boat's motion relative to the raft removes the current from the comparison. If the boat's speed relative to the water is \(v>0\), it moves away from the raft at speed \(v\) before turning and toward the raft at speed \(v\) afterward.

At the turn, the boat has some distance to make up relative to the raft. That distance is exactly the separation it created on the outward leg. Because its relative speed has the same magnitude on both legs, creating and closing this separation take equal amounts of time.

The two times total \(9\) hours, so the time from \(A\) to \(B\) was
\[
\frac92=\boxed{4.5\text{ hours}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
